items.html:
Use row-and-column equilibration in shared Lu, with optional retained scales:

[ E=RAC,\qquad Ax=b:\ x=C,E^{-1}(Rb),\qquad A^H\lambda=g:\ \lambda=R,E^{-H}(Cg). ]

R and C are positive real diagonals. Existing pullback −λ xᴴ stays unchanged; no derivatives of the numerical scaling are needed.

Fuse row/column maxima into current finite validation using max(abs(re), abs(im)). Healthy matrices return scales=None; no additional matrix scan or solve rescaling. Triggered matrices get reciprocal row maxima, followed by reciprocal maxima of row-scaled columns. Clamp reciprocals safely, reject zero rows/columns, and apply row and column factors sequentially. LAPACK’s equilibration uses this structure; its selection heuristic scales when factor spread exceeds 10× or magnitudes approach unsafe ranges.

Meaningful analytic check:

  • Choose non-Hermitian complex H = [[2+i, .5−.25i], [−.25+.5i, 3−i]], R=diag(2^-200,2^200), C=diag(2^100,2^-100), and A=R⁻¹HC⁻¹.
  • For arbitrary complex, multiple-column Y, construct b=R⁻¹HY; verify solved x=CY componentwise, so small coordinates cannot hide behind a norm dominated by large coordinates.
  • Independently choose complex Z, construct g=C⁻¹HᴴZ, and verify adjoint solve λ=RZ. This catches swapped rescaling and transpose/conjugate mistakes.

Similarity-only balancing cannot repair diagonal scale disparity; generic Lu needs independent row/column scaling. One equilibration sweep is reasonable, but cannot repair inaccurate translation coefficients or genuine physical singularity. No files edited or builds run.

items.html:
Normal/adjoint rescaling and implicit derivatives are mathematically correct. Two concrete extreme-range limitations remain:

  1. Column erasure during row scaling at linalg.rs:101: A=[[2^600,2^-600],[2^600,2^-599]], b=[1,2] has finite exact solution [0,2^600]. Row scaling underflows both second-column entries to zero, making the equilibrated operator singular.

  2. RHS overflow despite finite solution at linalg.rs:167: A=2^-600 * [[1,1],[1,-1]], b=[2^424,0] has finite exact solution [2^1023,2^1023]. Multiplication by R=2^600 overflows the first RHS entry.

Both are outside current exponent≤399 properties; standalone float arithmetic confirms the failing intermediate operations. No shared build run.

The prefilter also still performs a second matrix scan for well-conditioned matrices with isolated tiny entries, e.g. [[1,2^-100],[2^-100,1]]. Thus “no extra scan for healthy matrices” is narrower than stated; the resulting matrix and scales are nevertheless correct.

One actionable issue at linalg.rs:157: rayon::current_num_threads() initializes Rayon’s default global pool even when faer explicitly requests sequential execution. This creates unnecessary workers and prevents subsequent custom global-pool initialization.

Return Par::Seq immediately when faer’s degree is 1, before querying Rayon.

No other scheduling correctness issues found: normal/adjoint solves use matching scratch and execution settings, preserve rescaling, and respect both thread caps. WASM remains sequential. Read-only review; no builds or performance measurements.
